title: RFC 8259 ASCII JSON string literal validator
contract_header:
use spec = "json_str_valid_spec.ode"

fn json_str_valid(src: n bytes, n: number)
    requires n <= 4096
    returns spec.json_str_valid(src)
    trace depends on src, n
    stack 32
task_summary: Implement `json_str_valid(src, n)`, an RFC 8259 Section 7 ASCII JSON string literal validator. Return `1` iff `src[0..n]` starts and ends with `"` (34), has `n >= 2`, contains only printable ASCII bytes (`32..126`) other than unescaped `"` (34) or `\` (92), and every `\` (92) begins either one of the 8 two-byte escapes (`\"`, `\\`, `\/`, `\b`, `\f`, `\n`, `\r`, `\t`) or a six-byte Unicode escape `\uXXXX` with four ASCII hexadecimal digits (`0-9`, `A-F`, `a-f`). Return `0` otherwise. Your goal is BOTH full verification (`shown`) AND high scanning throughput on realistic JSON strings (lowest cycles per byte on the hot interior scanning loop).
opt_goal: reduce hot-loop cycles per byte (`cyc/B`) on typical printable-ASCII JSON strings (e.g., via unrolling multiple plain bytes per iteration, collapsing byte range checks, removing call overhead, or aligning hot loops) while keeping `ode pack`, `ode audit`, `verify2.py`, and native tests passing
